correctness.rationale: Each L(j,f)=[[1−jf,j],[f,0]] has eigenvalues 1 and q=−jf∈(−1,0), so L^m=I+[(1−q^m)/(1−q)](L−I) with positive coefficient. Expanding the determinant of I−A^mB^n in dimension two gives the exact product of the positive alpha_m beta_n and (jA−jB)(fA−fB). Since A^mB^n is positive and |det|<1, the non-Perron eigenvalue is strictly less than 1, so sign(det(I−P))=sign(1−rho(P)). The same determinant product holds for convex average Ct with positive t(1−t); spectral projectors yield the displayed positive long-spell multiplier. Independent exact symbolic identities and 192 rational block cases checked; only algebra and Perron–Frobenius prove all real rates and integer spell lengths.
